results.title: Frattini chief factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a Frattini chief factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and $A$ is contained in every maximal subgroup of $G$ that contains $B$; equivalently, $A/B \le \Phi(G/B)$, where $\Phi$ denotes the Frattini subgroup.

results.title: Complemented chief factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a complemented chief factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and some subgroup $M$ of $G$ satisfies $\langle M, A \rangle = G$ and $M \cap A = B$ (as $A$ is normal, the first condition says $MA = G$).

results.title: Ternary vectors
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the vectors of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/3$, that is, the functions from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ to $\mathbb{Z}/3$.

results.title: Multicolored sunflower
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a finite set of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$. Then $S$ contains a multicolored sunflower if there are triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with $x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

results.title: Multicolored sunflower conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: There are a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n > n_0$, every finite set $S$ of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ with $x + y + z = 0$ for every $(x, y, z) \in S$ and with $|S| \ge 3^{(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ contains a multicolored sunflower: triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with $x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

results.title: The multicolored sunflower conjecture holds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n > n_0$, every finite set $S$ of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ with $x + y + z = 0$ for every $(x, y, z) \in S$ and with $|S| \ge 3^{(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ contains a multicolored sunflower: triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with $x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

results.title: Square of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The square of a simple graph $G$ is the simple graph on the same vertex set in which two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when they are adjacent in $G$ or have a common neighbor in $G$, that is, a vertex $w$ adjacent in $G$ to both $u$ and $v$.

results.title: Adjacency in the graph square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ and vertices $u$ and $v$, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in the square of $G$ if and only if $u \ne v$ and either $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ or there is a vertex $w$ with $u$ adjacent to $w$ and $w$ adjacent to $v$ in $G$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the graph square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same vertex set such that every edge of $G$ is an edge of $H$. Then every edge of the square of $G$ is an edge of the square of $H$.

results.title: The square of a connected graph is connected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a simple graph $G$ is connected, then the square of $G$ is connected.

results.title: Adding edges preserves a Hamiltonian square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same finite vertex set such that every edge of $G$ is an edge of $H$. If the square of $G$ is Hamiltonian, then the square of $H$ is Hamiltonian.

results.title: Characterization of the graph square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same vertex set. Then $H$ equals the square of $G$ if and only if, for all vertices $u$ and $v$, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $H$ exactly when $u \ne v$ and either $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ or there is a vertex $w$ with $u$ adjacent to $w$ and $w$ adjacent to $v$ in $G$.

results.title: Skipping a vertex of a walk in the graph square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $u, w, v, x_1, \dots, x_k$ (with $k \ge 0$) be a sequence of vertices in which consecutive vertices are adjacent in $G$. If $u \ne v$, then in the sequence $u, v, x_1, \dots, x_k$ consecutive vertices are adjacent in the square of $G$.

results.title: A cyclic listing by square adjacencies gives a Hamiltonian square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_n$ be vertices with $n \ge 3$ and $v_0 = v_n$, such that $v_1, \dots, v_n$ are pairwise distinct and every vertex of $V$ is among them. If for each $i < n$ the vertices $v_i$ and $v_{i+1}$ are distinct and either adjacent in $G$ or have a common neighbor in $G$, then the square of $G$ is Hamiltonian.

results.title: Minimum degree in the square of a 2-connected graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a 2-vertex-connected simple graph on a finite vertex set with at least five vertices, every vertex has at least four neighbors in the square of the graph.

results.title: Open-addressing hash table
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $K$ be a type of keys, $V$ a type of values, $m$ a natural number, and $p$ a probe sequence assigning to each key $k$ and each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ a slot $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$. An open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$ consists of $m$ slots, each either empty or holding a single pair $(k, v)$ with $k \in K$ and $v \in V$.

results.title: Linear-probing probe sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a hash function $h : K \to \mathbb{N}$ and a number of slots $m > 0$, the $i$-th probe of a key $k$ is the slot $(h(k) + i) \bmod m$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.

results.title: Double-hashing probe sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given hash functions $h_1, h_2 : K \to \mathbb{N}$ and a number of slots $m > 0$, the $i$-th probe of a key $k$ is the slot $(h_1(k) + i \cdot h_2(k)) \bmod m$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.

results.title: Empty open-addressing table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The open-addressing table with $m$ slots and a given probe sequence in which every slot is empty.

results.title: Bounded lookup scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, a key $k$, a starting index $s$ and a budget $f$ of probes, examine the slots $p(k, s), p(k, s + 1), \dots$ in order, for at most $f$ probes. The scan returns the value bound to $k$ in the first examined slot that holds a binding for $k$, and returns no value if it first reaches an empty slot or exhausts the budget.

results.title: Lookup in an open-addressing table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, and let $k$ be a key. The lookup of $k$ in $T$ inspects the slots $p(k, 0), p(k, 1), \dots, p(k, m - 1)$ in this order. It returns the value $v$ of the first inspected slot that holds a pair $(k, v)$, and returns nothing if an empty slot is inspected first or if none of the $m$ inspected slots holds the key $k$.

results.title: Bounded insertion scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, a key $k$, a value $v$, a starting index $s$ and a budget $f$ of probes, examine the slots $p(k, s), p(k, s + 1), \dots$ in order, for at most $f$ probes. At the first examined slot that is empty or holds a binding for $k$, the scan returns the table with that slot overwritten by the binding $k \mapsto v$ and every other slot unchanged; if all $f$ examined slots…

results.title: Insertion into an open-addressing table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: To insert the binding $k \mapsto v$ into a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, examine the slots $p(k, 0), p(k, 1), \dots, p(k, m - 1)$ in order. At the first one that is empty or already holds a binding for $k$, write $k \mapsto v$ there, leaving every other slot unchanged, and return the updated table. If all $m$ examined slots hold bindings for other keys, the insertion fails and returns no table.

results.title: Valid open-addressing tables
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, where $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is the slot visited by the $i$-th probe of key $k$. Then $T$ is valid when it satisfies two conditions. Probe-closedness: whenever slot $j$ holds a binding $k \mapsto v$, there is an $i < m$ with $p(k, i) = j$ such that the slots $p(k, i')$ are occupied for all $i' < i$; this is what lets a lookup stop…

results.title: Stored binding in an open-addressing table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An open-addressing hash table $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$ when some slot of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$.

results.title: The empty open-addressing table is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all types $K$ and $V$, every number of slots $m$ and every probe sequence $p$, which assigns to each key $k$ and each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ a slot $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, the empty table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, in which every slot is vacant, is valid: it is probe-closed and no key is stored in two different slots.

results.title: Lookup in the empty open-addressing table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty open-addressing table returns no value.

results.title: Lookup after a successful open-addressing insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into an open-addressing hash table $T$ succeeds and yields the table $T'$, then looking up $k$ in $T'$ returns $v$. No validity assumption on $T$ is needed.

results.title: Insertion preserves validity of an open-addressing table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a valid table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, whose keys have decidable equality. If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ (adding it, or replacing the binding already stored for $k$) succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then $T'$ is valid: it is probe-closed and no key is stored in two different slots.

results.title: Open-addressing lookup returns only stored bindings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If looking up a key $k$ in an open-addressing hash table $T$ returns the value $v$, then $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$. No validity assumption is needed.

results.title: Lookup of an absent key fails
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing table and $k$ a key such that no slot of $T$ stores a binding $k \mapsto v$ for any value $v$. Then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns no value. No validity assumption on $T$ is needed.

results.title: Valid open-addressing tables find every stored key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a valid open-addressing hash table $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns some value.

results.title: Open-addressing lookup succeeds exactly on stored keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing hash table and $k$ a key. Looking up $k$ in $T$ returns a value if and only if $T$ stores a binding $k \mapsto v$ for some value $v$.

results.title: Bindings in a valid open-addressing table are unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a valid open-addressing hash table $T$ stores both $k \mapsto v_1$ and $k \mapsto v_2$, then $v_1 = v_2$.

results.title: Lookup in a valid table returns exactly the stored binding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing table, $k$ a key and $v$ a value. Then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of $T$.

results.title: Open-addressing insertion leaves other keys' bindings unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table, and suppose that inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ succeeds and yields the table $T'$. Then for every key $k' \neq k$ and every value $v'$, the table $T'$ stores $k' \mapsto v'$ if and only if $T$ stores $k' \mapsto v'$.

results.title: Insertion does not affect lookups of other keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing table and suppose inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ succeeds with result $T'$. Then for every key $k' \ne k$, looking up $k'$ in $T'$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$.

results.title: Failed open-addressing insertion finds every probed slot taken
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$. If inserting a binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ fails, then for every $i < m$ the slot $p(k, i)$ holds a pair $(k', v')$ with $k' \neq k$.

results.title: Collision count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and keys $x, y \in \alpha$, the collision count of $x$ and $y$ in $H$ is the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$.

results.title: Universal hash family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ is universal if $m > 0$, $H$ is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$ the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$, multiplied by $m$, is at most $|H|$; that is, $x$ and $y$ collide under at most a $1/m$ fraction of the members of $H$.

results.title: Indexed universal hash family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set of indices from a type $\iota$, and let $h$ assign to each index $i \in \iota$ a function $h_i$ from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$. The family $h$ is universal on $s$ if $m > 0$, $s$ is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$ the number of indices $i \in s$ with $h_i(x) = h_i(y)$, multiplied by $m$, is at most $|s|$.

results.title: Collision count is at most the family size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and all keys $x, y \in \alpha$, the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$ is at most $|H|$.

results.title: A key collides with itself under the whole family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and every key $x \in \alpha$, the collision count of $x$ with itself in $H$ equals $|H|$: $x$ collides with itself under every function in $H$.

results.title: The empty hash family is not universal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type of keys $\alpha$ and every natural number $m$, the empty family of functions $\alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is not universal: universality includes nonemptiness, since its meaning is a bound on the collision probability for a uniformly chosen member.

results.title: The empty indexed family is not universal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every index type $\iota$, every type of keys $\alpha$, every natural number $m$ and every family $(h_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of functions $h_i \colon \alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, the family is not universal over the empty index set: indexed universality includes nonemptiness of the index set, since there is no uniform random choice from an empty family.

results.title: The empty family satisfies the collision bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$ and all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in a set $\alpha$, the collision count of $x$ and $y$ in the empty family of functions from $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$, multiplied by $m$, is at most the size of the empty family, which is $0$.

results.title: Mod-prime hash function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$ and elements $a, b$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b} \colon \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is $h_{a,b}(x) = \operatorname{val}(ax + b) \bmod m$, where $ax + b$ is computed in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $\operatorname{val}(z)$ is the canonical natural-number representative of $z$ (the residue in $\{0, \dots, p - 1\}$…

results.title: Mod-prime index set
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, the index set of the mod-prime family is the set of pairs $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$.

results.title: Indexed mod-prime family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$, the indexed mod-prime family assigns to each index $(a, b)$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b} \colon \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.

results.title: Mod-prime family of distinct functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $p > 0$ and $m > 0$, the mod-prime family is the finite set of all functions $h_{a,b}$ from $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$, where $h_{a,b}$ is the mod-prime hash function with index $(a, b)$.

results.title: Value of the mod-prime hash
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$ and elements $a, b, x$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the mod-prime hash value $h_{a,b}(x) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, read as a natural number, equals $\operatorname{val}(ax + b) \bmod m$. results.title: The pair map of the mod-prime family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and fix two keys $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. The pair map at $x$ and $y$ sends an index $(a, b)$ of the mod-prime family, that is, $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a \ne 0$, to the pair $(ax + b, ay + b) \in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^2$ of inner hash values at $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Evaluating the pair map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number, let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $(a, b)$ be an index of the mod-prime family, so that $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$. Then the pair map at $x$ and $y$ sends $(a, b)$ to $(ax + b, ay + b)$.

results.title: The pair bijection is given by the pair map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \neq y$ be elements of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. For every index $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, the image of $(a, b)$ under the pair bijection for $x, y$, viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, is the value of the pair map at $(a, b)$, namely $(ax + b, ay + b)$.

results.title: The pair map is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \ne y$ be keys in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then the pair map at $x$ and $y$, which sends an index $(a, b)$ of the mod-prime family (so $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$) to $(ax + b, ay + b)$, is injective.

results.title: Number of mod-prime indices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive natural number $p$, the set of pairs $(a, b)$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a \neq 0$ has exactly $p(p - 1)$ elements.

results.title: Universality of the mod-prime family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $m$ a positive natural number. The indexed mod-prime family, whose member at the index $(a, b)$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, is the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b}$, is universal over the set of all such indices: this set is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \neq y$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the number of indices $(a, b)$ with $h_{a,b}(x) = h_{a,b}(y)$,…

results.title: Members of the mod-prime family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p > 0$ and $m > 0$. A function $h$ from $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ belongs to the mod-prime family of distinct functions exactly when $h = h_{a,b}$ for some index $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$, where $h_{a,b}$ is the mod-prime hash function with index $(a, b)$.

results.title: Marginal on a set of coordinates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $n$ a natural number and $\mu$ a real-valued function on the strings $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \alpha^n$. For a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of coordinates, write $x|_S : S \to \alpha$ for the restriction of a string $x$ to $S$. results.title: Joint entropy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $\alpha$, a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $\mu$ on $\alpha^n$, the full (joint) entropy of $\mu$ is $H(\mu) = -\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) \log \mu(x)$, where $\log t$ is the natural logarithm of $|t|$ for $t \neq 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

results.title: Marginal entropy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $\alpha$, a natural number $n$, a real-valued function $\mu$ on $\alpha^n$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of coordinates, let $P_S$ be the marginal of $\mu$ on $S$: for $y \in \alpha^S$, $P_S(y)$ is the sum of $\mu(x)$ over the $x \in \alpha^n$ whose restriction to $S$ is $y$. results.title: Marginals of a nonnegative function are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$, and $S$ a set of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the marginal $P_S$ of $\mu$ on $S$ satisfies $P_S(y) \ge 0$ for every $y \in \alpha^S$.

results.title: Marginals preserve total mass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$, and $S$ a set of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the marginal $P_S$ of $\mu$ on $S$ satisfies $\sum_{y \in \alpha^S} P_S(y) = 1$.

results.title: Monotonicity of marginal entropy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$. If $T \subseteq S$ are sets of coordinates in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on $T$ is at most the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on $S$.

results.title: Submodularity of marginal entropy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a probability mass function on $\alpha^n$, that is, $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$ and $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$. Writing $H_S$ for the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of coordinates, any two such sets $A$ and $B$ satisfy $H_{A \cup B} + H_{A \cap B} \le H_A + H_B$.

results.title: Marginal entropy on the empty set vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, $n$ a natural number, and $\mu$ a real-valued function on $\alpha^n$ with $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} \mu(x) = 1$. Then the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on the empty set of coordinates is $0$.

results.title: Marginal entropy on all coordinates is the full entropy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite set $\alpha$, a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $\mu$ on $\alpha^n$, the marginal entropy of $\mu$ on the set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of all coordinates equals the full entropy of $\mu$.
